q: 1. The minimum percentage of silica, alumina and ferric oxide in lime for white washing, is ............
explain: Lime used for white-washing (Fat Lime) should be as pure as possible (high calcium oxide content), meaning the percentage of impurities like silica, alumina, and iron oxide should ideally be zero.

q: 2. The initial setting time of hydraulic lime, is ............
explain: Unlike cement, hydraulic lime sets much slower. Its initial setting time is generally taken as 120 minutes (2 hours).

q: 3. The burning of bricks in kilns is complete within ............ hours.
explain: The actual burning process in a kiln typically takes about 24 hours (one full day) to reach the required temperature and complete the chemical transformation of clay.

q: 4. The bricks after burning in kilns require about ............ days to cool down for unloading.
explain: Sudden cooling makes bricks brittle. To maintain quality, they are allowed to cool gradually for about 12 days before unloading.

q: 5. Quick lime is a ............
options: Product left immediately after the calcinations of pure limestone
explain: Quick lime (CaO) is the caustic product obtained by the calcination (heating) of limestone. Option 'b' is also chemically correct, but 'c' describes its production process as a material.

q: 6. The consistency test is performed to find ............
explain: The standard consistency test (using Vicat's apparatus) determines the percentage of water required to produce a cement paste of standard viscosity for other tests.

q: 7. The seven day compressive strength of a good Portland cement, as obtained from the compressive test on cement-sand mortar cubes, should not be less than ............
explain: For standard OPC, the 7-day compressive strength should be at least 17.5 N/mm² (175 kg/cm²).

q: 8. Surkhi is added to lime mortar to ............
explain: Surkhi (ground burnt clay) is a pozzolanic material. When added to lime, it reacts to give the mortar hydraulic properties (ability to set in damp conditions).

q: 9. Soundness of cement is tested by ............
explain: The Le-Chatelier apparatus is specifically used to measure the expansion (soundness) of cement caused by free lime.

q: 10. Soundness test of cement determines ............
explain: Soundness refers to the ability of cement to maintain its volume. An 'unsound' cement expands due to excess free lime or magnesia.

q: 11. In a mortar, the binding material is ............
explain: Mortar consists of a binding material (like cement or lime) and an inert material/fine aggregate (like sand).

q: 12. The durability of cement concrete is usually improved by
options: increasing the quantity of coarse sand
decreasing the proportion of fine aggregate
explain: As Per book Key B. But as per google Decreasing the water-cement ratio reduces the porosity of the hardened cement paste, which significantly enhances the durability of the concrete.

q: 13. The shrinkage of concrete ......... its bond strength.
explain: Slight shrinkage helps the concrete 'grip' the reinforcement more tightly, effectively increasing the bond strength between the steel and concrete.
Quick lime is chemically known as Calcium Oxide (CaO). It is obtained by the calcination of limestone (CaCO3).

q: 15. Quick setting cement is produced by adding ...............
options: less amount of gypsum in very fine powdered form
more amount of gypsum in very fine powdered form
aluminum sulphate in very fine powdered form
pozzolana in very fine powdered form
explain: Gypsum acts as a retarder. By reducing the gypsum content, the cement sets much faster than Ordinary Portland Cement.

q: 16. In lime manufacturing, if the fuel is allowed to have direct contact with lime, then the kiln is called ...............
explain: In a flame kiln (also known as an intermittent kiln), the fuel and limestone are in direct contact, which allows for higher temperatures but can sometimes result in impurities from the fuel ash.

q: 17. The type of glass used to make laboratory equipment and cooking utensils is ...............
explain: Borosilicate glass (like Pyrex) has a low coefficient of thermal expansion, making it highly resistant to thermal shock during heating.

q: 18. Water glass is ...............
options: water formed by condensation on glass
solution of sodium silicate in water
explain: Water glass is the common name for sodium silicate (Na2SiO3) solution, which is used as a binder and for fireproofing.

q: 19. A badly mixed cement concrete results in ...............
explain: Honeycombing refers to voids in concrete caused by a lack of mortar to fill the spaces between coarse aggregates, often due to poor mixing or placement.

q: 20. Seasoning of timber is essential to remove ...............
explain: Seasoning is the process of drying timber to reduce its moisture (sap) content to a level compatible with its intended use.

q: 21. A piece of sawn timber whose cross-sectional dimensions exceed 5 cm... is called a ...............
explain: A baulk is a piece of timber that has been roughly squared and has dimensions larger than 5 cm on each side.

q: 22. The trunk of tree left after cutting all the branches is known as ...............
explain: Once a tree is felled and the branches are removed, the remaining main stem is referred to as a log.

q: 23. Good quality cement contains higher percentage of ............
explain: Tricalcium silicate (C3S) is responsible for the early strength of cement. Higher percentages indicate a high-quality, high-strength cement.

q: 24. Initial setting of cement is caused due to ............
explain: Tricalcium aluminate (C3A) reacts fastest with water and is primarily responsible for the initial flash set of the cement.

q: 25. The central part of a tree is called ............
explain: The pith (or medulla) is the innermost central core of the tree, consisting of soft cellular tissue, around which the annual rings are formed.

q: 26. The solvent used in cement paints is ..........
explain: Cement paints are water-based; water acts as the vehicle and solvent to facilitate the hydration of the cement base.

q: 27. The purpose of seasoning of timber is to ..........
explain: The primary goal of seasoning is to reduce the moisture content (sap) of the timber to a level appropriate for its intended use.

q: 28. A badly mixed cement concrete may lead to .............
explain: Honeycombing in concrete refers to voids, cavities, and coarse, stony surface areas caused by mortar failing to fill the spaces between coarse aggregate.

q: 29. The type of steel used for precision leveling staff, is .............
explain: Invar is an alloy of steel and nickel with a very low coefficient of thermal expansion, ensuring that the precision of the leveling staff is not affected by temperature changes.

q: 30. For the manufacture of stainless steel, steel is mixed with .............
explain: Chromium is the essential alloying element in stainless steel, providing the corrosion resistance by forming a passive oxide layer.

q: 31. Slacking of lime is affected by ............
explain: Slaking is the chemical process of adding water to quicklime (CaO), which converts it into hydrated lime [Ca(OH)2] with the evolution of heat.
Snowcem is a well-known brand of waterproof cement paint used for exterior surfaces.

q: 33. The hydraulic lime which resembles very much with Portland cement in its chemical composition is called ............
explain: Because of its high silicate content, eminently hydraulic lime has properties similar to cement, especially its ability to set without air.

q: 34. Poor or lean lime ............
options: slakes rapidly with considerable evolution of heat
takes very long time to develop adequate strength
explain: As per Key D but As per google Lean lime has slow slaking and setting times and develops strength much more slowly than fat or hydraulic lime.

q: 35. The process of adding the required quantity of water to quick lime in order to convert it in hydrated lime, is known as ............
explain: Slaking is the controlled hydration of CaO to form Ca(OH)2. If water is added to a large mass, it is often called slaking.

q: 36. Quick lime on reaction with water gives ............
explain: The product of the slaking process (CaO + H2O) is calcium hydroxide, commonly known as slaked lime.

q: 37. The calcinations of pure lime result in ............
explain: The calcination of pure limestone (calcium carbonate) at high temperatures, typically above , removes carbon dioxide and results in the production of quick lime, also known as caustic lime or burnt lime

q: 38. The variety of pig iron used for manufacture of wrought iron, is ............
explain: White forge pig iron is typically used for the production of wrought iron through the puddling process.

q: 39. According to I.S. 399 - 1963, the weight of the timber is specified at ............
explain: Standard weight specifications for timber are measured at a 12% moisture content level, which represents seasoned wood.

q: 40. In lime manufacturing, if the fuel is not allowed to have direct contact with lime, then the kiln is called............
explain: In a flare kiln (also called an intermittent kiln), the fuel is burnt in a separate firebox so the flame reaches the lime without direct coal contact.

q: 41. The compound of Portland cement which contributes to the strength after two to three years is ............
explain: Di-calcium silicate (C2S) hydrates very slowly and contributes to the long-term gain in strength of the concrete over years.

q: 42. Lime stones are generally known as ............
explain: Limestone is sedimentary (formed by deposition), aqueous (formed in water), and stratified (occurs in layers).
